newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock funds resume sharp inflows - survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock funds resume sharp inflows - survey.

text.p: Cash flows into U.S. equity funds rose to $843 million for the two-day period ended January 20 versus inflows of $350 million for the three-day period ended January 16, according to Mutual Fund Trim Tabs.

If the current trend persists, "equities have a chance to best the all-time record inflow of $28.9 billion (for U.S. and international) in January 1996," the fund tracking firm said in its twice-weekly newsletter.
The firm said flows into international funds rose to $235 million from $90 million.
Aggressive growth funds saw a turnaround to inflows of $138 million from outflows of $57 million, while growth funds posted inflows of $278 million versus outflows of $19 million.
Growth and income funds recorded lower inflows to $378 million from $509 million.

Bond funds recorded outflows of $132 million versus inflows of $533 million. Muni funds had outflows of $245 million versus inflows of $291 million, the firm said. Government/GNMA funds posted outflows of $26 million versus inflows of $297 million. Corporate/income/global funds had inflows of $24 million versus outflows of $162 million.
